requirements.note: The basics, so you do not start badly.
What each level needs to unlock.

rules.title: What we wish someone had told us on day one
rules.text: Nine things in order of importance. New on 770, start right here.
rules.imageAlt: Clan member pointing at the house rules

items.title: Your HQ
items.text: Your base. The higher it is, the more you unlock. HQ level lets you take heroes five levels above it, sets the maximum level for every other building, and raises the daily raid limit on other bases. Priority number one.

items.title: Resources
items.text: Food, wood and metal produce themselves or come from mines and raids. The genuinely hard ones are Zenith, the special currency, and laboratory badges. Look after those two.

items.title: Trucks
items.text: Only send the orange ones, top quality. You do not lose troops if they get stolen, so there is no real risk. Send them one at a time with your best escort army. They can be stolen twice at most.

items.title: Mines
items.text: Farmed outside your base. In the daily Mine Battle event you look for Gold and Crystal mines, and Crystal is hero experience. You start with three attacks a day and later get four. You can spend diamonds to detect new ones. Tip, at night send your second and third armies to mine and keep the first one free.

items.title: Heroes
items.text: They level with experience, best during happy hour. Weapons are levelled with other material weapons, without spending iron, thinking ahead to the weekly VS. There are three factions in a cycle, Wings of Dawn, Blood Rose, and Guardians of Order. It does not affect your opponent, it affects your own army bonus. Three of the same faction give 105% attack, three plus two mixed give 107%, four the same give 110%, and five the same give 115%, the holy grail.

items.title: Troops
items.text: Trained in the barracks, they attack and defend. Each faction is tied to one troop type, and that barracks sits behind the matching faction building, which you have to unlock first. Blood Rose gives Raiders, Wings of Dawn gives Shooters, and Guardians of Order gives Motorcyclists.

items.title: Events
items.text: Total Preparation, Zombie Boss, Arena. They give extra rewards and are not mandatory, but they speed things up a lot. The next guide covers them one by one.

items.title: HQ Chest
items.text: It fills on its own for up to eight hours. After that it stops accumulating, so do not leave it full. It gives resources and free hero weapons. The easiest thing to collect every day.

items.title: Pro tips
items.text: Alliance donations, when you donate technology hold the button down instead of tapping one by one, that is how you get critical donations of x2, x5, x10, and once even x270. To move around the map, when a helicopter appears find the nearest allied base, reinforce it, and leave from there, because you travel three times faster between allied bases. And on village resources, upgrading production buildings above level 16 or 17 is not worth it, since attacking a single enemy player gives you more than twenty four hours of production.

board.title: Vehicle modules, no mystery
board.text: For server 770, season 1. We have no idea what this is yet, but we want to be ready.

posts.title: First, let us not mix things up
posts.text: If you already know that blueprints and wrenches are the normal vehicle upgrades, perfect, that still exists and is not what we explain here. Modules are a separate system.

posts.title: What a module is
posts.text: Think Fast and Furious. You take a car that is already good and tune it further with engine, wheels, body, performance. Modules are that, applied to the Last Z vehicle. There are six types, Radar, Wheels, Armour, Solar Battery, Nitro, and Artillery. No need to memorise them, just understand that the vehicle carries modules, they give extra stats, and they can be upgraded.

posts.title: Where they come from
posts.text: Trucks can carry component chests. In the alliance shop, the Random Module Box Lv.1 costs 4,500 alliance coins and gives a random Lv.1 exterior module. They also show up in events, shops, activity rewards, and various chests. There is no single source.

posts.title: What to do with them
posts.text: You combine them. Three identical modules of the same level give one of the next level. A Lv.2 module needs 3 of Lv.1, a Lv.3 needs 9, a Lv.4 needs 27, and a Lv.5 needs 81. And that is for one module type only. With several types at once you see why so many resources are needed.

posts.title: And components
posts.text: A different resource within the vehicle system. They also come from chests, trucks, events, and rewards. Module and component are not the same thing, treat them as different resources until we see the full interface.

posts.title: And chips
posts.text: They exist, and they are not components under another name either. Three separate resources, modules, components, and chips. Chips have their own progression, but since 770 is still in season 1 and we do not have the full interface, we will not invent explanations taken from other servers that may run another version. When the chip screen shows up, we will explain it.

posts.title: When to spend all this
posts.text: The Alliance Duel event has a Modded Vehicle Boost day, the famous vehicle day. That day you score points using component chests, chip chests, blueprints, wrenches, and certain radar tasks. Opening a chest during the event gives the resource plus points. Opening it any other day gives only the resource. So save your resources for vehicle day.

posts.title: What we do on 770 right now
posts.text: We are in season 1, the system is not fully unlocked, and that is fine. The mission is not to be experts yet, it is to recognise this stuff and not waste it. Module box, keep. Components, keep. Chips, keep. Truck with related chests, take it. Module box in the shop, judge if it is worth it. Blueprints and wrenches, save for vehicle day. Something new you do not understand, do not touch.

posts.title: The most important rule
posts.text: Do not open things just because. Faced with a new chest, ask first what it is, what it does, whether it scores in any event, whether you need it now, and whether it is worth keeping. If you do not know, keep it and look later, it does not expire in your inventory.

posts.title: Summary for the most lost member
posts.text: Modules are parts to tune a vehicle that is already built. Several types, each with its own bonuses. You get them from trucks, chests, shops, events, and rewards. You upgrade them by combining identical ones of the same level. Components are another resource, chips are yet another. All of this is separate from the normal blueprint and wrench upgrades. There is a specific Alliance Duel day for the vehicle, so save up. We do not need to be first to understand it, we need to be the ones who say, we have had this saved since season 1.

join.title: Get into the clan
join.text: If you play on server 770 and want a clan where things get explained, look us up in game. And if you spot something wrong in a guide, say so and it gets fixed.
